thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: LyraHealth (enterprise, VPC) — sustained 429 spike observed from dedicated pool lyra-prod-1. error-rate=78% over last 5m, approx qps drop; page sent to #incidents and @eng-oncall.

eng-oncall: Paging SRE on-call — I'm on it. Pulling logs and current pool metrics.

sara: grabbing pool metrics now. It looks like a sudden surge from a handful of client IPs inside the VPC, plus a backlog of long-running requests holding KV cache. Dedicated pool max-concurrency hit.

adrian: Confirmed: lyra-prod-1 has saturated GPU workers. Autoscale didn't trigger due to recent manual scale lock (ticket #SC-842). There's a manual override preventing new nodes.

maria: I'm with the account team on the call with LyraHealth. They say they launched a scheduled batch that should have been internal but hit prod endpoints (~11:05 UTC). Their ops can kill job if we need immediate relief.

eng-oncall: Plan options: 1) ask Lyra to stop the batch (fast), 2) remove manual scale lock to let autoscale add capacity (requires infra signoff), 3) route a portion of traffic to hosted fallback for a short window (needs ops/network), 4) temporary rate-limit increase / contract exception for Lyra (billing/account). We should do 1+2+3 in parallel. Thoughts?

kevin: From account perspective we can approve emergency contract bump for 2 hours to allow extra QPS on dedicated, but need exec sign-off. I can get it within 10–15m.

nikhil: Runtime note — routing to hosted will require switching their route policy to "fallback-hosted" which is ready but we need to flip the tenant mapping. It will also send traffic out of their VPC. Need explicit approval from Lyra ops (they normally prohibit egress).

maria: Lyra ops on the line: they can kill the batch in ~5 minutes, but prefer we add short breathing room first while they confirm job termination. They explicitly requested we avoid egress due to compliance.

adrian: If egress is blocked we can't route to hosted. So we need to either lift the scale lock now or apply a temporary QPS uplift on the dedicated pool. I can remove the scale lock if SRE/eng-oncall authorize. That will allow autoscale to add nodes within ~3 minutes.

eng-oncall: Authorize removal of manual scale lock. Sara, coordinate with Adrian to watch node join. Maria, let Lyra ops know we're going to remove the lock; ask them to hold off on killing the batch until we see capacity coming up.

sara: Removing lock now (I have the key). Running command:
```
./infractl scale-lock unlock --pool lyra-prod-1 --by=sara --reason="emergency dedicated saturation"
```

ops-bot: infractl: unlock request accepted. Change-id: CHG-11829. Autoscaler will resume.

adrian: Nodes provisioning started. Expected ready ~ 3-4m. I'm also temporarily raising per-tenant qps threshold on the pool to tolerate a smoother ramp:
```
./poolctl update --pool lyra-prod-1 --tenant lyra --qps-cap 3000 --duration 2h
```

eng-oncall: Noted — we should document this as an emergency temporary exception and set a rollback. Kevin, proceed with the contract note so billing flags it for the two-hour window.

kevin: I've logged internal billing note: BILL-EMG-LYRA-17698. Approving emergency uplift for 2h. I'll follow up with formal amendment.

maria: Lyra ops: we removed the lock and raised threshold. Can you confirm egress still disallowed? They confirm no egress; they will not accept hosted fallback. They're going to terminate the batch if we don't see improvement in 6m.

nikhil: Early signs: error-rate falling to ~30% as new nodes join and KV cache warms. KV eviction spikes seen — we should increase small cache window for Lyra to reduce misses for next 10 minutes.

sara: Applying cache tweak:
```
./runtimectl cache update --tenant lyra --kv-window 45s --prefetch=true
```

ops-bot: runtimectl: cache update accepted. Job-id: JOB-7621.

eng-oncall: Monitoring. Cross-team note: this is a coordinated emergency mitigation (scale unlock + qps uplift + cache tweak). We still need a proper postmortem and a change to avoid manual scale-locks on critical dedicated pools.

maria: Lyra ops: they confirm traffic is back to normalish, error-rate ~4% now. They will still finish cancelling the batch within 10 minutes and want a written incident summary. Account exec (kevin) to follow up with customer comms.

adrian: Rolling back temporary qps uplift at timestamp T+2h (automated). I'll file infra change to prevent scale-locks on production dedicated pools: CHG-11830.

kevin: I'll draft customer note and include usage impact and temporary billing adjustment. Sending to Lyra legal for compliance note.

nikhil: Action items: 1) postmortem ticket PT-4729 assigned to sara; 2) infra change CHG-11830 to remove manual lock capability; 3) billing note BILL-EMG-LYRA-17698; 4) runtime config JOB-7621; 5) follow-up sync with Lyra ops tomorrow.

sara: Creating postmortem doc and will include metrics, timeline, and recommended safeguards (quota guards, auto-unlock policy, tenant isolation limits).

eng-oncall: Closing this thread as mitigated. If Lyra sees any reoccurrence, reopen or create new page. Great cross-team response — :tada:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Mitigated. Root-cause: scheduled customer batch hitting prod endpoints + manual scale-lock preventing autoscale. Remediation: manual scale-lock removed, temporary qps uplift, cache tweaks, customer killed batch. Postmortem assigned to sara (PT-4729).
